p.src: Now, as Song Jiang looked about him from horseback, he saw ambushed troops on every side. He ordered the men to fight their way along the main road, but then heard that five bodies of troops had blocked it. Everyone began crying out in dismay. Song Jiang asked, “Why are you crying out?” The soldiers all replied, “The road ahead is a maze. After making a complete circuit, we have come back here again.” Song Jiang said, “Have the troops make for the torchlight. There must be houses and people there, and we can find a way out.” They had not gone much farther when another shout arose from the vanguard: “We had only just managed to head toward the torchlight when we found the ground covered with sharpened bamboo stakes, iron caltrops, and chevaux-de-frise, blocking every entrance!” Song Jiang said, “Can it be that Heaven means to destroy me?” Just as he was in a state of desperate alarm, a commotion broke out among Mu Hong’s company in the left wing, and a report came: “Shi Xiu is here.” Song Jiang looked and saw Shi Xiu, saber in hand, rushing up before his horse. “Brother, do not panic. I have discovered the way. Pass the order secretly through the five divisions: whenever they see a poplar tree, they are to turn there, without regard to whether the path is broad or narrow.” Song Jiang urged his men and horses onward, turning whenever they saw a poplar. After Song Jiang had traveled some five or six li, he saw ever more men and horses gathering ahead. Growing suspicious, Song Jiang summoned Shi Xiu and asked, “Brother, why are there so many enemy troops ahead?” Shi Xiu replied, “They use a lantern as their signal.” From horseback, Hua Rong spotted it and pointed it out to Song Jiang. “Brother, do you see that bowl-shaped lantern among the shadows of the trees? Whenever we head east, they draw the lantern eastward; and whenever we head west, they draw it westward. That alone, I believe, is how they signal their orders.” Song Jiang asked, “What can we do about that lantern?” Hua Rong replied, “What difficulty is there in that?” He took up his bow, nocked an arrow, and spurred his horse forward. Aiming into the shadows, he loosed a single shaft, which flew unerringly and struck down the bowl-shaped red lantern. When the ambushed troops on every side could no longer see the red lantern, they all fell into confusion. Song Jiang told Shi Xiu to lead the way while they fought their way out through the village entrance. Then shouts arose one after another from the hills ahead, while a long line of torches surged chaotically in every direction. Song Jiang ordered the vanguard to halt and sent Shi Xiu ahead to scout the way. Before long, he returned and reported, “It is the second contingent from our mountain stronghold. They have come to support us and have scattered the ambushers.” On hearing this, Song Jiang advanced and attacked from both sides. His forces seized a path and rushed out through the village entrance, while the troops of the Zhu Family Manor scattered in all directions; then he joined forces with Lin Chong, Qin Ming, and the others, and together they encamped at the village entrance. By then dawn had broken. They established a fortified camp on high ground and mustered the troops, only to discover that Huang Xin, the “Guardian of the Three Mountains,” was missing. Song Jiang was greatly alarmed and asked what had happened. A soldier who had accompanied Huang Xin the previous night came forward and said, “Chief Huang obeyed your order and went ahead to scout the road. Without warning, two hooked poles shot out from the reeds and swept his horse’s legs from under him. Five or seven men seized him alive, and we were unable to rescue him.” Song Jiang flew into a rage on hearing this and wanted to execute the soldiers who had accompanied him. “Why did you not report this sooner?” Lin Chong and Hua Rong dissuaded Song Jiang. The men said in distress, “We have failed to take the manor and instead lost two of our brothers. What are we to do now?” Yang Xiong said, “There are three allied villages here. Master Li of the eastern village was shot by that scoundrel Zhu Biao the other day and is now recuperating at his manor. Why do you not go and consult him, brother?” Song Jiang said, “I had quite forgotten him. He will know the lay of the land here and its strengths and weaknesses.”

p.src: He ordered a pair of bolts of satin, a sheep, and wine to be prepared, together with a fine horse, saddle, and bridle, intending to call in person and request an audience. Lin Chong and Qin Ming were left temporarily in charge of the fortified camp. Taking Hua Rong, Yang Xiong, and Shi Xiu with him, Song Jiang mounted his horse and set out for the Li Family Manor, accompanied by three hundred cavalrymen.

p.src: When they reached the manor, they found its gatehouse tightly shut and its drawbridge raised high, while numerous manor guards and horsemen were arrayed behind the walls. Drums were already beating atop the gatehouse. From horseback, Song Jiang called out, “I am Song Jiang, a man of honor from Liangshan Marsh. I have come expressly to pay my respects to your master and have no other purpose. There is no need to stand on guard.” Du Xing, watching from the manor gate, saw Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu among them. He hurriedly opened the gate and sent a small boat across, then greeted Song Jiang respectfully. Song Jiang hastily dismounted and returned his greeting. Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu stepped forward and explained, “This brother is the man who introduced the two of us to Master Li. He is called Du Xing, the ‘Demon Face.’” Song Jiang said, “So you are Steward Du. May I trouble you to tell Master Li that I, Song Jiang of Liangshan Marsh, have long heard of his great name but have never had the good fortune to pay him a visit. Now, because the Zhu Family Manor has chosen to oppose us, I have passed this way and brought a modest gift of colored satin, a fine horse, a sheep, and wine. I ask only for an audience and have no other intention.”

p.src: Having received the message, Du Xing crossed back into the manor and went straight to the main hall. Li Ying, still wounded, sat on his bed wrapped in a quilt. Du Xing told him that Song Jiang wished to see him. Li Ying said, “He is a rebel from Liangshan Marsh. How can I meet with him? It would only invite suspicion that we had some private understanding. Go back and tell him only that I am ill in bed and unable to move, so it is difficult for me to receive him. I shall pay him a visit another day. As for the gifts he has bestowed, I dare not accept them.”

p.src: Du Xing crossed over again to see Song Jiang and reported, “My master repeatedly sends his respects to you, Chief. He had meant to come and welcome you in person, but regrettably he has been wounded and lies ill in bed, so he cannot meet you. On another day he will call upon you expressly. As for the generous gifts just bestowed upon him, he dares not accept them.” Song Jiang said, “I understand your master’s intentions. Because I suffered defeat attacking the Zhu Family Manor, I sought an audience with him; but he fears offending the Zhu Family Manor and refuses to come out and meet me.” Du Xing said, “That is not so. He truly is ill. Though I am a native of Zhongshan, I have lived here for many years and know a good deal about the true circumstances of this region. In the center stands the Zhu Family Manor, to the east our Li Family Manor, and to the west the Hu Family Manor. The three villages swore a bond of life and death, pledging to aid one another in times of trouble. But this time the Zhu family has angered my master, so he will not go to their aid. I fear only that the Hu Family Manor in the western village may come to assist them. Nothing else at their manor need concern you, but they have one woman warrior named Hu Sanniang, called ‘Ten Feet of Steel.’ She wields a pair of Sun-and-Moon sabers and is extraordinarily formidable. She is betrothed to Zhu Biao, the Zhu family’s third son, who is to marry her before long. If you generals mean to attack the Zhu Family Manor, you need not guard against the east; you need only keep strict watch on the western road. The Zhu Family Manor has two gates, one at the front of Lone Dragon Ridge and one behind it. Attacking the front gate alone will accomplish nothing. You must assault from both sides before you can break through. When the fighting at the front gate grows fierce, the tangled roads are hard to distinguish. Everywhere are winding paths of varying width. Wherever there is a white poplar, turn the corner there; that is a passable road. If there is no such tree, it is a dead end.” Shi Xiu said, “They have now cut down all the white poplars. What can we use as markers?” Du Xing said, “Though they have felled the trees, how could they remove every root? The stumps must still be there. You should attack only by daylight; do not advance at night.”

p.src: After hearing him out, Song Jiang thanked Du Xing and led his men and horses back to camp. Lin Chong and the others came to meet them, and all sat down in the main encampment. Song Jiang told the chiefs that Li Ying had refused to meet him and repeated what Du Xing had said. Li Kui broke in, “We kindly sent him gifts, yet that scoundrel would not come out to welcome our elder brother! I’ll take three hundred men, smash open that damned manor, grab the rogue by the hair, and drag him out to pay his respects to our brother.” Song Jiang said, “Brother, you do not understand. He is a wealthy, respectable commoner who fears the authorities. How could he rashly consent to meet men like us?” Li Kui laughed. “The fellow must be a little child, afraid to see strangers.” Everyone burst out laughing together. Song Jiang said, “Be that as it may, two of our brothers have been trapped, and we do not know whether they are alive or dead. All you brothers must exert your utmost and advance with me to attack the Zhu Family Manor again.” They all rose and said, “Who would dare disobey our elder brother’s command? Whom will you order to go?” Li Kui, the Black Whirlwind, said, “If you are afraid of that little child, I’ll go.” Song Jiang said, “You brought ill fortune as vanguard. I have no use for you this time.” Li Kui lowered his head and swallowed his anger. Song Jiang then selected Ma Lin, Deng Fei, Ou Peng, and Wang the Short-legged to accompany him as he personally led the vanguard. For the second detachment he named Dai Zong, Qin Ming, Yang Xiong, Shi Xiu, Li Jun, Zhang Heng, Zhang Shun, and Bai Sheng, readying men for operations by water; for the third he named Lin Chong, Hua Rong, Mu Hong, and Li Kui, dividing them into two supporting columns. Once all the troops had received their assignments, they ate their fill, donned their armor, and mounted their horses.

p.src: Before Lone Dragon Mountain rises Lone Dragon Ridge; upon Lone Dragon Ridge stands the Zhu Family Manor. A long stream winds around the ridge; encircling it on every side are drooping poplars. Within the walls, swords and halberds stand in grim ranks; before the gates, sabers and spears are densely arrayed. All who meet the foe are valiant warriors; all who hold the van are youthful men. Zhu Long in battle is truly hard to defeat; none can withstand Zhu Hu when weapons cross; And Zhu Biao is yet more skilled in arms; his thunderous shouts rival the Hegemon-King’s. Elder Zhu is rich in stratagems; he owns a thousand chests of gold, silver, gauze, and silk. A pair of white banners stands before the gate, plainly bearing these two lines: ‘Fill in the marsh and seize Chao Gai; trample down Mount Liang and capture Song Jiang.’

p.src: There on horseback, Song Jiang read the two banners of the Zhu Family Manor and flew into a rage. He swore, “If I cannot take the Zhu Family Manor, I shall never return to Liangshan Marsh.” When the chiefs saw them, they too were enraged as one. When Song Jiang heard that the troops behind had all arrived, he left the chiefs of the second detachment to attack the front gate. He himself led the vanguard around to the rear of Lone Dragon Ridge to inspect the Zhu Family Manor, whose defenses behind were as impregnable as walls of bronze and iron and were kept in perfect order. As he watched, a body of troops suddenly appeared due west, charging from the rear with battle cries. Song Jiang left Ma Lin and Deng Fei to hold the Zhu Family Manor’s rear gate, while he took Ou Peng and Wang the Short-legged with half the troops to meet the attackers. p.src: Golden hairpins press down her cicada-wing tresses; phoenix slippers rest aslant in jeweled stirrups. Linked armor is lined with crimson gauze; an embroidered sash girds the slender waist that sits so straight. With frosty blades she hacks through valiant troops; with delicate jade hands she captures fierce generals alive. A natural beauty like a crabapple blossom—‘Ten Feet of Steel’ rides foremost into battle.

p.src: The approaching troops were led by Hu Sanniang, the woman warrior of the Hu Family Manor known as “Ten Feet of Blue.” Mounted on a blue-maned horse and brandishing a pair of Sun-and-Moon sabres, she led three to five hundred retainers to reinforce the Zhu Family Manor. Song Jiang said, “We were just speaking of the formidable woman warrior at the Hu Family Manor. This must be she. Who dares engage her?” Before he had finished speaking, Wang the Short Tiger, a notorious lecher, heard that the opponent was a woman and imagined he could capture her in a single bout. With a shout, he spurred forward, leveled the spear in his hand, and rode out to meet her. Both armies raised a battle cry. Hu Sanniang urged on her horse and whirled her sabres against Wang the Short Tiger—the one masterful with twin blades, the other outstanding with a single spear. After they had fought more than ten rounds, Song Jiang watched from horseback and saw that Wang the Short Tiger’s spear could no longer parry her attacks. When Wang the Short Tiger first saw “Ten Feet of Blue,” he could hardly wait to seize her. But after more than ten rounds, to his surprise, his hands began to tremble, his legs went numb, and his spearwork fell entirely into disorder. Though they were locked in mortal combat, Wang the Short Tiger began behaving frivolously toward her. “Ten Feet of Blue” was quick-witted and thought, “What an insolent brute!” She drove in upon him, hacking straight up and down with both sabres. How could Wang the Short Tiger withstand her? He wheeled his horse and was about to flee when “Ten Feet of Blue” galloped after him. Hooking up the sabre in her right hand, she lightly extended her ape-like arm, lifted him clean out of his carved saddle, and carried him off alive. The retainers all surged forward and dragged Wang the Short Tiger away sideways and backward. A poem bears witness:

p.src: Seeing Wang Ying captured, Ou Peng leveled his spear and came to the rescue. “Ten Feet of Blue” urged on her horse, crossed her sabres before her, and met Ou Peng in combat. Ou Peng came from a family of military men and wielded an iron spear superbly. Watching him, Song Jiang secretly applauded. Yet for all Ou Peng’s mastery of the spear, he could gain not the slightest advantage over the woman warrior. From afar, Deng Fei saw that Wang the Short Tiger had been captured and that Ou Peng could not overcome the woman warrior. He galloped forward, whirling an iron chain and shouting at the top of his voice. The men of Zhu Family Manor had been watching for some time and, fearing that “Ten Feet of Blue” might come to harm, hurriedly lowered the drawbridge and opened the manor gate. Zhu Long personally led more than three hundred men out, spurring his horse and carrying his spear, intent on capturing Song Jiang. Seeing him, Ma Lin rode out wielding his twin sabres and intercepted Zhu Long in battle. Fearing for Song Jiang’s safety, Deng Fei stayed close beside him as fighting raged on both sides and cries of battle rose one after another. Song Jiang saw that Ma Lin was no match for Zhu Long and Ou Peng could not defeat “Ten Feet of Blue.” Just as he was growing alarmed, a body of cavalry suddenly charged in from the flank. When Song Jiang saw who it was, he rejoiced. It was Qin Ming, the “Thunderbolt,” who had heard the fighting behind the manor and come to reinforce them. Song Jiang shouted, “Commander Qin, take Ma Lin’s place!” Qin Ming was hot-tempered by nature; moreover, the Zhu Family Manor had captured his disciple Huang Xin, so he was already in a foul rage. He spurred his horse, swung up his wolf-toothed mace, and charged straight at Zhu Long. Zhu Long likewise leveled his spear and met Qin Ming. Ma Lin led his men away to recover Wang the Short Tiger. When “Ten Feet of Blue” saw Ma Lin coming to rescue the prisoner, she abandoned Ou Peng and turned to engage Ma Lin. Both were skilled with twin sabres. As they met on horseback, their blades were like jade fragments whirled by the wind and jeweled blossoms scattered through snow; Song Jiang’s eyes blurred as he watched. Meanwhile, after Qin Ming and Zhu Long had fought more than ten rounds, Zhu Long could no longer withstand him. From within the manor gate, the instructor Luan Tingyu mounted his horse with an iron hammer at his side, leveled his spear, and charged out. Ou Peng came forward and intercepted Luan Tingyu in combat. Luan Tingyu did not close with him; checking his spear, he veered off and fled diagonally. Ou Peng pursued him, but Luan Tingyu hurled his flying hammer and struck him squarely, sending him tumbling head over heels from his horse. Deng Fei shouted, “Lads, save him!” Whirling his iron chain, he charged straight at Luan Tingyu. Song Jiang urgently called the lesser bandits to rescue Ou Peng and remount him. Unable to withstand Qin Ming, Zhu Long spurred his horse and fled. Luan Tingyu also abandoned Deng Fei and came to fight Qin Ming. Suddenly the trip rope was pulled taut; as he tried to turn back, men shouted from both sides and hooked poles came down in a tangled mass. He was captured alive in the saddle. p.src: One was Yang Xiong, the “Sickly Guansuo,” and the other Shi Xiu, the “Desperate Third Son.” From the northeast another gallant shouted loudly, “Leave those men to me!” Song Jiang looked and saw that it was Hua Rong, the “Little Li Guang.” The forces from all three directions arrived together. Song Jiang was overjoyed, and they joined strength to fight Luan Tingyu and Zhu Long. The watchers at the manor feared the two might be overwhelmed. They ordered Zhu Hu to guard the manor gate, while the young master Zhu Biao mounted a fierce horse, took up a long spear, and personally led more than five hundred men out from behind the manor to join the general melee. At the front of the manor, Li Jun, Zhang Heng, and Zhang Shun crossed through the water, but a hail of arrows from the manor prevented them from making an attack. Dai Zong and Bai Sheng could only raise battle cries from the opposite bank. Seeing that evening had fallen, Song Jiang urgently ordered Ma Lin to escort Ou Peng out through the village entrance first. Song Jiang then ordered the lesser bandits to beat the gong and gather all the gallants together as they fought their way back.

p.src: Song Jiang himself rode about searching everywhere, fearing that his brothers might lose their way. As he rode on, “Ten Feet of Blue” suddenly came galloping after him. Taken by surprise, Song Jiang spurred his horse and fled eastward. “Ten Feet of Blue” pressed close behind. The eight hooves clattered like cups overturning and cymbals scattering as they raced deep into the village. Just as “Ten Feet of Blue” caught up with Song Jiang and was about to strike, someone on the hillside shouted, “You damned wench! Where do you think you’re chasing my brother?” Song Jiang looked and saw the “Black Whirlwind” Li Kui, brandishing two broad axes and striding rapidly toward them at the head of seventy or eighty lesser bandits. “Ten Feet of Blue” reined her horse around and headed toward the edge of the woods. p.src: Firmly he wears his jewel-studded helmet; once more he dons his polished silver armor. Flowering branches are embroidered on his white silk robe; his lion-buckled belt is thickly set with fine jade. He grips an eighteen-foot serpent spear; beneath him his frost-dappled steed neighs again and again. Throughout the hills they call him Little Zhang Fei: he is Lin Chong, the Panther Head.

p.src: The newcomer was none other than Lin Chong, the Panther Head. From horseback he shouted, “Hey, woman! Where do you think you’re going?” Hu Sanniang, the Ten-Foot Blue, brandished her blades and spurred straight at Lin Chong, who leveled his eighteen-foot serpent spear to meet her. Before they had fought ten bouts, Lin Chong feigned an opening and let the Ten-Foot Blue slash in with both blades. He checked them with his serpent spear, forcing the blades aside; then, closing in, he lightly stretched out an ape-like arm, deftly twisted her supple waist, and with a single tug seized her alive and dragged her across his saddle. Song Jiang saw it and cried out in praise, hardly knowing the extent of his delight. Lin Chong ordered the soldiers to bind her, then galloped forward and asked, “Were you hurt at all, elder brother?” “I wasn’t hurt,” Song Jiang replied. He then told Li Kui to hurry into the village and support their comrades, directing them to assemble at the village entrance for consultation. Night had already fallen, and they must not prolong the fighting. The Black Whirlwind led his men away. Lin Chong guarded Song Jiang and, with the Ten-Foot Blue held captive on horseback, made his way out to the village entrance. That evening none of the chieftains gained the advantage, and all hurried out to the village entrance. The troops of the Zhu Family Manor also withdrew to their stronghold. Throughout the village, the dead were beyond counting. Zhu Long ordered all the captives placed in prison carts. Once Song Jiang too was seized, he intended to send them under guard to the Eastern Capital and claim a reward. Hu Family Manor had already sent Wang Ying under guard to Zhu Family Manor.

p.src: Now Song Jiang withdrew his main force and established a stockaded camp at the village entrance. First he had the Ten-Foot Blue brought before him, then summoned twenty steady, experienced followers under four officers and mounted them on four swift horses. He had her hands bound and placed her on another horse, saying, “Take her to Liangshan Marsh this very night. Deliver her into the custody of my father, Lord Song, and then return to report to me. When I return to the stronghold, I shall decide what is to be done with her.” All the chieftains assumed that Song Jiang wanted the woman for himself, and they took the utmost care in sending her away. He also had Ou Peng sent up the mountain first in a cart to recuperate. They all received their orders and departed that very night. That night Song Jiang sat brooding in his tent. He did not sleep a wink, but remained seated until dawn.

p.src: The next day a scout came to report that the strategist Scholar Wu was approaching with the three Ruan brothers, Lü Fang, and Guo Sheng, leading five hundred men and horses. On hearing this, Song Jiang went out of camp to welcome the strategist Wu Yong, then seated him in the central command tent. Scholar Wu had brought wine and food. He drank a toast with Song Jiang to congratulate him, while provisions and rewards were distributed among all the officers and troops. Wu Yong said, “Chieftain Chao at the stronghold has repeatedly heard that your earlier attack went badly, elder brother, so he specially sent me and five chieftains to aid you in battle. How have victory and defeat gone in recent days?” “It is a long story,” Song Jiang replied. Those cursed rogues of the Zhu family have raised two white banners over their manor gate, bearing the words: ‘Fill in the marsh and seize Chao Gai; trample Liangshan and capture Song Jiang.’ The scoundrels are intolerably insolent. In our first attack, we lacked the advantage of the terrain and lost Yang Lin and Huang Xin. When we advanced again last night, the Ten-Foot Blue captured Wang Ying, Luan Tingyu wounded Ou Peng with his mace, and trip ropes brought down Qin Ming and Deng Fei, who were then taken prisoner. With defeat upon defeat like this, had Instructor Lin not chanced to capture the Ten-Foot Blue alive, all our fighting spirit would have been crushed. Now that matters have come to this, what are we to do? If I, Song Jiang, cannot break Zhu Family Manor and rescue these brothers, I would sooner die here. I would have no face to return and see Elder Brother Chao Gai.” Scholar Wu laughed. “Zhu Family Manor is indeed fated to be defeated by Heaven, for just such an opportunity has arisen. As I see it, the place can be broken within a day or two.” Song Jiang was astonished and overjoyed at these words. He hurriedly asked, “How can Zhu Family Manor be broken within a day or two? Where has this opportunity come from?” Scholar Wu smiled and, without the least haste, raised two fingers together and revealed the opportunity. Truly, it was a hand thrust forth into the sky to seize the clouds, rescuing men from the all-encompassing net of Heaven and Earth. What opportunity did the strategist Wu Yong reveal? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
